questions.prompt: A box holds years 1 through 100. Where does year 101 go?
questions.explanation: The first box is full at year 100. Year 101 starts the second group of one hundred years.

questions.prompt: The 19th century runs from 1801 to 1900. Which century contains 1900?
questions.explanation: 1900 is the last year of the 19th century. The next century starts in 1901.
The 20th century ended in 2000. The next year, 2001, began the 21st.

title: Which century is a year in? Think of boxes of 100

sources.name: US Naval Observatory — The 21st century and 3rd millennium

practice: Try History Quiz and see which periods you recognise.

sections.html:
A century is a period of one hundred years. When we say “the first century”, we mean the first numbered group of one hundred years.

Imagine a box that holds 100 year cards. Put cards 1, 2, 3 and so on into it. Card 100 fills the last space. Card 101 must go in the next box.

The second box holds years 101 to 200. The third holds 201 to 300. Each box is one century.
sections.title: One century holds one hundred years

sections.html:
Following the same pattern, the nineteenth box starts at 1801 and finishes at 1900. That is the 19th century.

The twentieth box starts with the very next card: 1901. It finishes at 2000.

It feels odd because 1900 and 1901 both start with “19”. But one is the last card in a full box, and the other is the first card in a new one.
sections.title: Why 1900 belongs in the nineteenth box

So the 21st century began in 2001. The year 2000 was the final year of the twentieth box.
sections.title: Three boxes you will often meet

sections.html:
The 16th century runs from 1501 to 1600. Where should the next year, 1601, go?

Open the next box

Into the 17th century. The old box finished with 1600, so 1601 starts a new one.

You may see CE after a year. It means “Common Era”; AD is another label used for the same year numbering. In this numbering, the first century begins with year 1, not year 0.

This article uses those year numbers. Dates marked BCE or BC describe earlier years and need a separate explanation.
